RcppOptimLib — Implementation Plan

Source: IMPLEMENTATION.md

An R interface to OptimLib, Keith O’Hara’s header-only C++ library of numerical optimization methods (BFGS, L-BFGS, CG, gradient descent, Newton, Nelder–Mead, differential evolution, PSO, SUMT constrained optimization, and root finding), built on Armadillo. The package follows the Rcppautodiff / RcppEnsmallen model: ship the headers in inst/include/ so client packages can use LinkingTo: RcppOptimLib, plus a small set of R-callable wrappers.

Status

Phase 0 and most of Phase 1 are done and verified: the package compiles against Rcpp 1.1.2 / RcppArmadillo 15.4.2.1 on R 4.6.1 (Linux, gcc 13), and all 10 tinytest tests pass (BFGS and DE with C++ objectives; BFGS and Nelder–Mead with R-function callbacks).

Key design decisions (already implemented)

  1. Flat header layout. OptimLib’s headers use include paths relative to the library root ("misc/optim_structs.hpp", "BaseMatrixOps/include/BaseMatrixOps.hpp"), so they sit directly in inst/include/ — not in a subdirectory. LinkingTo puts exactly one directory (<pkg>/include) on the compiler search path, and this is the only layout that works for client packages without patching every include in the library.

  2. inst/include/RcppOptimLib.h is the single entry point. It defines OPTIM_USE_RCPP_ARMADILLO (OptimLib then includes <RcppArmadillo.h> itself — without this flag, RcppArmadillo’s and system Armadillo’s configurations mix and fail to link) and OPTIM_DONT_USE_OPENMP, then includes optim.hpp. Because the defines live in the header rather than in src/Makevars, client packages inherit them automatically.

  3. OpenMP is off by default. OptimLib auto-enables OpenMP whenever _OPENMP is defined, and its parallel metaheuristics (DE, PSO) evaluate the objective from worker threads. R’s C API is single-threaded, so an R-function callback objective under OpenMP would crash the session. A client package that uses only pure C++ objectives may opt back in by defining RCPPOPTIMLIB_ALLOW_OPENMP before including RcppOptimLib.h and adding $(SHLIB_OPENMP_CXXFLAGS) to its own Makevars.

  4. Two patches to the vendored code:

    • Index-vector typedefs (marked [RcppOptimLib patch] in misc/optim_options.hpp): ColVecUInt_t/RowVecUInt_t changed from arma::Col<unsigned long long> to arma::Col<arma::uword>. On LP64 Linux arma::uword is unsigned long, a distinct type from unsigned long long, and Armadillo ≥ 12 index-vector overloads (X.rows(uvec), X(uvec)) reject the upstream type. Worth offering upstream as a PR.
    • Console output: std::cout/std::cerr/printf replaced mechanically (sed) with Rcpp::Rcout/Rcpp::Rcerr/Rprintf across the headers — CRAN forbids compiled code writing to stdout/stderr, and R CMD check flags the symbols even when the print paths are disabled at runtime. Also pruned: BaseMatrixOps/.git, .github/ and tests/ (hidden-file NOTE and a GNU-Makefile WARNING in check).
    • Upstream bug fixes (0.0.2; each marked RcppOptimLib patch in the source, all present on upstream master as of 2026-11 and worth reporting/PRing):
      • unconstrained/lbfgs.hpp: x was not advanced to x_p after the first line search, so the first in-loop curvature pair used an s spanning two steps against a one-step y; L-BFGS stalled after 2 iterations on Rosenbrock. The first-step grad_err also used the initial gradient instead of grad_p.
      • unconstrained/pso_dv.hpp: the stagnation-reset Hadamard product mixed a column vector (rand_vec) with a row vector (P_max - P_min); Armadillo throws at runtime.
      • constrained/sumt.hpp: penalty gradient was c * colSums(J) instead of c * t(J) %*% g, inconsistent with the penalized objective; BFGS stalled once the penalty grew (x + y <= 2 test stopped at 1.00046 instead of 1).

    Known upstream behaviours not patched, handled on the R side: de_prmm halves the population three times (hard-coded) and indexes with unsigned arithmetic, so n_pop %/% 8 <= n_pop_best reads out of bounds — optimlib() validates this. With check_freq = Inf, de reports success after n_gen generations but de_prmm/pso/pso_dv report failure — documented in ?optimlib.

  5. Licensing. The package is GPL (>= 3) (Apache-2.0 is compatible with GPL-3 but not GPL-2); the bundled OptimLib and BaseMatrixOps headers are Apache-2.0, Copyright Keith O’Hara, who is listed in Authors@R as aut, cph. See inst/COPYRIGHTS, inst/include/optimlib-LICENSE and inst/include/optimlib-NOTICE.txt.

Vendored version / regeneration recipe

Bundled: OptimLib master commit 5453f48 (2024-04-28) with BaseMatrixOps submodule commit 9e5beec, generated in header-only mode. To upgrade:

git clone https://github.com/kthohr/optim.git && cd optim
git submodule update --init
./configure --header-only-version        # inlines the .cpp sources
# then replace the contents of inst/include/ (keep RcppOptimLib.h,
# optimlib-LICENSE, optimlib-NOTICE.txt) with header_only_version/*

After regenerating, re-apply the patches from decision 4 (the ColVecUInt_t typedefs, the console-output sed, and the BaseMatrixOps pruning) if not fixed upstream, and record the new commit hashes here.

# console-output patch, run from inst/include/:
files=$(grep -rl 'std::cout\|std::cerr\|printf(' --include='*.hpp' --include='*.ipp' .)
sed -i 's/std::cout/Rcpp::Rcout/g; s/std::cerr/Rcpp::Rcerr/g; s/\bprintf(/Rprintf(/g' $files
rm -rf BaseMatrixOps/.git BaseMatrixOps/.github BaseMatrixOps/tests

Phase 2 — a real R-level interface

Goal: one optimlib() front end resembling stats::optim():

Phase 3 — client-package story and docs

Phase 4 — CRAN readiness

Known risks / open questions

  • Windows support (see Phase 4) — the main unknown.
  • optim::lbfgs terminates early on the classic Rosenbrock test from (-1.2, 1): it stalls at (-1.017, 1.069) even with iter_max = 2000 and tight tolerances, while optim::bfgs reaches (1, 1) on the identical objective (verified 2026-08-24 against the bundled commit). Investigate the upstream convergence check before exposing lbfgs through the Phase 2 R interface; add cross-algorithm convergence tests on standard problems (Rosenbrock, Beale, Wood).
  • Upstream activity: the bundled commit is from April 2024; upstream moves slowly, so the uword patch may need to live here long-term.
  • de_prmm/pso_dv variants call the objective from OpenMP regions even in some serial builds — audit before exposing them to R callbacks.
  • BaseMatrixOps trailing niceties: stats/ headers in the bundle include sampling helpers not needed for optimization; they compile fine but could be pruned to shrink the install footprint.
